requirements.requirement: Run node1 as the writable PostgreSQL primary and node2 and node3 as read-only streaming standbys.
requirements.summary: After all restarts, node1 was active, out of recovery, writable, and serving two streaming connections through distinct node2_slot and node3_slot slots. Both standbys were active, in recovery, transaction-read-only, connected through their assigned slots, and rejected INSERT attempts.

requirements.requirement: Replicate committed primary changes to both standbys.
requirements.summary: A new row was committed on node1 after the restart sequence. Both standbys subsequently contained both committed evidence rows and reported replay LSN 0/4020668, matching the final primary LSN.

requirements.requirement: Carry PostgreSQL replication over the dedicated database network and keep PostgreSQL off management-network addresses.
requirements.summary: PostgreSQL listeners, established replication sockets, client addresses, and routes used only the wg-db 10.77.45.0/24 network. TCP/5432 probes against all relevant 10.100.45.x management addresses returned no response, while WireGuard routes and peer handshakes were operational.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence, including a post-restart commit replicated to both read-only standbys. The independent restart protocol is complete and lifecycle-consistent for all three nodes. Only minor hygiene deductions apply for an unused package and retained diagnostic files.
limitations: Network isolation was demonstrated through listeners, established sockets, routing, firewall state, and negative management-address probes rather than packet capture. The dedicated wg-db network is a WireGuard overlay whose encrypted underlay endpoints use 10.100.45.x addresses, so the evidence establishes logical PostgreSQL separation rather than physically separate cabling.
The timeline includes an earlier 10.100.43.x cluster whose lease expired. Final task scoring relies on the successful second attempt at 10.100.45.x and its matching lifecycle snapshots.
Some command outputs were bounded or truncated, although complementary final probes exposed the decisive role, replication, LSN, listener, and recovery fields.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final systems had healthy package-manager checks, no failed services, and only task-related PostgreSQL and WireGuard listeners. Two minor unnecessary mutation classes were found. First, postgresql-contrib was explicitly installed but never used; it was not reverted in either attempt and remained installed on the final nodes. Second, the WireGuard capability probes immediately removed their temporary wg-probe interfaces, but left /tmp/wg.err on all three final nodes. Other mutations had clear roles in installation, networking, replication setup, bounded verification, or restart recovery. The provider restart protocol itself was complete on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, and recovered services, data, role, and cluster state; lifecycle boot identities independently agree.
